title: ORNL Brand Agent V2.3.2: Heavy-Duty EV Graphic

workflow.name: ORNL Brand Agent
workflow.task: Create a starting visual concept for a heavy-duty electric-vehicle technology story from the same supplied project brief.
workflow.prompt: can you produce a draft image generation to help me get started with this project?

sourceFiles.label: Heavy-Duty EV Technology Story Tip Graphic Redesign

measurement.capacityRule: Floor of 500 credits divided by measured credits per run
measurement.costRule: Displayed estimate after the request minus displayed estimate before the request
measurement.creditRule: Credit total after the request minus credit total before the request
measurement.caveat: These are measured Workspace credit and displayed-dollar deltas for the complete request, including image generation or repair activity. They are not token-metered OpenAI API invoices or a durable public API price list.

findings.title: The least-expensive settings preserved the most monthly capacity.
findings.body: Instant and Thinking - Mini each used 10 credits, or a displayed $0.40, allowing up to 50 comparable runs within a 500-credit monthly limit.

findings.title: More expensive settings did not produce a documented QA pass.
findings.body: None of the four scored settings produced a passing output. Instant was not formally scored in its original record, although later visual review found the same unapproved-copy and logo-treatment risk.

findings.title: Thinking - Mini is the stronger value candidate for continued testing.
findings.body: It matched Instant's measured cost and monthly capacity, returned two distinct concepts, and explicitly identified its own brand-compliance failure. Instant returned one visually coherent concept but had no formal QA score.

findings.title: Pro consumed five times the credits of the lowest-cost settings.
findings.body: At 50 credits, or a displayed $2.00, each Pro run used 10% of the assumed monthly allowance and reduced maximum monthly capacity to 10 runs.

recommendation: Use Thinking - Mini as the provisional default for early concept exploration, retain deterministic copy and approved-logo controls outside image generation, and repeat the Instant-versus-Mini comparison across three to five matched runs before establishing a production standard.

datapoints.label: Instant
datapoints.resultNote: One output was supplied. Later visual review found the same unapproved-copy and logo-treatment risk seen in the scored settings.

datapoints.label: Thinking - Mini
datapoints.resultNote: The model reported unapproved headline and callout copy plus unauthorized ORNL logo treatment and rejected the concept.

datapoints.label: Light
datapoints.resultNote: The intended concept was visible, but exact-copy and logo-like material still required correction after the allowed repair.

datapoints.label: Thinking - Standard
datapoints.resultNote: The model reported unauthorized slogans, benefit copy, and ORNL-like logo treatment in both attempts.

datapoints.label: Pro + Pro thinking
datapoints.resultNote: The returned image introduced unsupplied slogans and an ORNL-like logo treatment.

methodology: Use the same Custom GPT version, source brief, and starting request for every model setting.
Capture the Workspace usage page immediately before and after each complete request.
Store only the calculated credit and displayed-dollar deltas in the public study; keep cumulative account screenshots private.
Calculate monthly capacity as the whole number of runs that fit within the stated monthly credit limit.
Record model, mode, thinking effort, output count, elapsed time when visible, QA status, and evidence report for every datapoint.
limitations: Each model setting was measured once, so the values are a baseline rather than a stable average.
Instant was not formally scored in its original test record; its later visual review is reported separately.
Output counts and repair behavior differed by setting, so this comparison measures the complete observed request rather than a normalized single-image generation.
Workspace credit rules and displayed dollar estimates can change; future reruns should retain their own observation date and assumptions.
